title: Credit Card Fraud: Who Pays When Your Card is Stolen?

faq.q: What is "zero liability" in credit card fraud?
faq.a: Zero liability means you are not responsible for any financial loss from unauthorised credit card transactions, typically when the fraud is due to bank negligence, a third-party breach, or if you report it within three working days of notification.

faq.q: How quickly must I report credit card fraud to the bank?
faq.a: You should report any unauthorised transaction or loss of card immediately. To ensure zero liability, the RBI guidelines state you must report it within three working days of receiving communication from the bank about the transaction.

faq.q: What happens if I report fraud after seven working days?
faq.a: If you report the fraud after seven working days from the date of receiving communication from the bank, your liability will be determined by the bank's board-approved policy. This often means you may bear the full loss incurred until the time of reporting.

faq.q: Can I be held liable if I shared my PIN with someone?
faq.a: Yes, if the loss is due to your own negligence, such as sharing your PIN, CVV, or OTP, you will be liable for the entire loss until the unauthorised transaction is reported to the bank.

faq.q: What kind of communication from the bank triggers the reporting timeline?
faq.a: The timeline for reporting fraud begins from the date you receive communication from the bank about the unauthorised transaction. This usually refers to SMS alerts or email notifications sent by the bank.

faq.q: Should I block my card immediately if it's lost, even if I don't see fraud?
faq.a: Absolutely. Blocking your card immediately upon realising it's lost or stolen is the best preventive measure. This stops any potential fraudulent transactions before they occur, protecting you from liability.
